slides.title: A Physics-Consistent Benchmark for Contact-Rich Human-Robot Interaction in Assistive Care
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for contact-rich assistive tasks, such as robot-assisted bathing, emphasizing physics-aware screening over simple task success. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A physics-consistent benchmark for assistive care showing that task completion doesn't guarantee physically valid contact.
card.key_idea: Combines a deformable, passively responding human model calibrated via manikin force-indentation measurements with physics-aware scoring and a leak-free, vision-only observation protocol.
card.evaluation: Evaluated State Machine, VoxPoser, and $\pi_{0.5}$ across 7 bathing tasks (140 runs/method) using peak force, joint-limit margins, and task success.
card.limitation: Uses a medical manikin instead of human tissue; upper-arm simulation reuses forearm calibration; limited to a single robotic-bathing scenario.

slides.title: FWBC-VLA: Force-Aware Whole-Body Compensation for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation
slides.highlight: This framework integrates a sensorless residual-torque estimator with a vision-language-action model to enable wheeled-legged robots to perceive and compensate for physical interaction forces during contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: FWBC-VLA enables contact-rich loco-manipulation using sensorless force estimation for VLA action and body compensation.
card.key_idea: HSR-Force estimates interaction residuals from proprioception, which are fused as tokens into a VLA policy and used by a compensation generator for whole-body stabilization.
card.evaluation: Tested on whiteboard wiping and door opening tasks using the WL&Arm dataset; outperformed baselines like OpenVLA and ForceVLA in success rates.
card.limitation: The impact of force estimation accuracy on overall task performance requires further investigation.

slides.title: A Wearable Pneumatic Device for Continuous, Closed-Loop, Bidirectional Tactile Interaction
slides.tldr: WEARABLE PNEUMATIC DEVICE FOR BIDIRECTIONAL TACTILE INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This wearable pneumatic system integrates sensing and actuation to enable real-time bidirectional tactile interaction, improving teleoperated manipulation performance and reducing mental workload.

card.one_liner: A wearable pneumatic device enabling bidirectional tactile interaction by using the same modality for sensing and feedback.
card.key_idea: Distributed closed-loop controllers with proportional piezoelectric valves regulate textile pouches, allowing real-time wireless transmission of pressure signals between a robot and a human operator.
card.evaluation: Tested via device characterization (34.2Hz bandwidth) and human studies (n=25). Results show improved teleoperation: 23.1% lower pressure, 27.4% faster tasks, and 18.1% lower mental demand.
card.limitation: Weight discrimination accuracy dropped significantly in complex 3-element teleoperated tasks; some users conflated robotic system latency with haptic device delay.

slides.title: SpectraTac: A Compact Camera-Free Optical Tactile Sensor with Distributed Color Sensing
slides.tldr: CAMERA-FREE OPTICAL TACTILE SENSOR FOR 3D FORCE AND CONTACT ESTIMATION
slides.highlight: SpectraTac provides a low-cost, compact alternative to camera-based tactile sensing by using distributed color sensors to estimate 3D force and contact regions.

card.one_liner: SpectraTac is a compact, camera-free optical tactile sensor using distributed color sensing for force estimation.
card.key_idea: Combines active RGB illumination with three distributed RGBC sensors and a PDMS layer to decode 3D force and contact regions via a multitask ResMLP framework.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a six-axis F/T sensor; achieved 99.9% contact-region accuracy and 3D force MAEs between 0.161N and 0.429N. Results appear trustworthy.
card.limitation: Future work is needed to improve spatial resolution, force decoupling, dynamic tactile perception, and long-term robustness.

slides.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
slides.tldr: FOUNDATION MODEL FOR SUB-MILLIMETER CONTACT-RICH ASSEMBLY
slides.highlight: Facet-0 utilizes a joint action-wrench proposal and a distributional Action-Wrench Critic to manage contact consequences, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on force-based skill acquisition and precise manipulation.

card.one_liner: Facet-0 is a robotic foundation model for sub-millimeter assembly that predicts and values contact consequences.
card.key_idea: It uses flow-matching to jointly generate action chunks and predicted wrist-wrenches, refined by a distributional Action-Wrench Critic and bounded local adaptation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five computer-assembly tasks using ManuFacet-1K; achieved 82% mean success vs 15% for the strongest baseline with 0.5mm accuracy.
card.limitation: The hardest task (LEVER), consisting only of contact-critical presses, remained the most challenging with only 50% success.

slides.title: Scaling Bimanual Household Manipulation from 1,500 hours of Demonstrations to On-Policy Corrections
slides.tldr: BIMANUAL MANIPULATION SCALING VIA VLA MODELS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a large-scale bimanual demonstration dataset and a VLA model that improves through real-time human interventions, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on skill acquisition and human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: XR-2 VLA model scales bimanual household manipulation using 1,500 hours of demonstrations and DAgger corrections.
card.key_idea: A 5B parameter VLA model combining Qwen3-VL and a flow-matching action expert, trained on expert teleoperation and UMI data, then refined via failure-weighted DAgger corrections.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on clothes-folding; success rates rose from 34% (30h expert data) to 84% (120h) and further to 93% after three DAgger rounds.
card.limitation: Expert data gains saturate around 120 hours, requiring human-in-the-loop corrective data to resolve remaining deployment-time failures.

slides.title: CometVLA: Co-Training on an Embodied Data Pyramid towards Physical Understanding
slides.tldr: IMPROVING VLA MODELS VIA EMBODIED PHYSICAL VQA
slides.highlight: CometVLA utilizes an embodied physical VQA corpus and a data pyramid to improve physical understanding in manipulation tasks, supporting RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: CometVLA improves robot manipulation by co-training a VLA model on an embodied physical VQA pyramid.
card.key_idea: Uses CometData (embodied VQA) and Global Action Prior (GAP) tokens to bridge VLM physical reasoning with a diffusion-based action expert via a learnable information bottleneck.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on RoboTwin simulation and real-world G1 robot tasks; outperformed baselines like π0.5 and showed positive correlation between CometBench VQA and success rates.
card.limitation: Correlation analysis had a narrow range of success rates, and real-robot testing covered only a limited subset of manipulation behaviors.

slides.title: Anomaly Detection on Small Industrial Components via Vision-Based Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: TACTILE ANOMALY DETECTION FOR SMALL COMPONENTS
slides.highlight: This research explores vision-based tactile sensing for detecting geometry-driven defects, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception of physical states.

card.one_liner: Systematic evaluation of unsupervised anomaly detection using vision-based tactile sensing for small industrial components.
card.key_idea: Benchmarked four feature-embedding methods (SPADE, PaDiM, FAPM, InReaCh) using a GelSight Mini sensor to detect geometric defects via contact imprints on five real-world components.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using AUROC, AUPRC, and AUC-PRO@0.01 on a custom tactile dataset; tested nominal sample counts, cross-position generalization, and image resolution.
card.limitation: Soft-interface gel wear limits the number of possible acquisitions, and the dataset is not publicly released due to confidentiality.
